name: Equinox EQX ARC + Equinox+ app
role: EQX ARC women's health program team (via Equinox PR)
why: EQX ARC is Equinox's women's training program for cycle health through perimenopause; coaches personalise plans from Oura overnight data (sleep, HRV, resting heart rate), and the Equinox+ app reads heart rate and biometrics from Apple HealthKit. A defined, coach-led use for overnight HR, HRV and sleep.
why_now: Equinox announced a Women's Health Advisory Board to support EQX ARC on 2026-05-04, and the Equinox+ app shipped again on 2026-10-14. The program is expanding its data-informed coaching in 2026.
warm_path: None known; pr@ is the published contact. Ask to be routed to the EQX ARC product or partnerships lead.
ask: Route a short note to the EQX ARC product lead and share whether they would review early SDK docs for a second overnight data source.
opener: Hi Equinox team, congratulations on the EQX ARC Women's Health Advisory Board in May. Your coaches already plan around overnight sleep and HRV, so I'd be glad to send early SDK docs and sample overnight data once ready, in case a second data source helps members who don't wear a ring. I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. We're building a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. Could you forward this to whoever leads EQX ARC product? https://calendly.com/jeremy-vybe/30min
opportunity: Second overnight HR/HRV/sleep source for EQX ARC coaching, next to Oura.

name: Estrogen, Garmin-measured sleep and ADHD feasibility study (Jessica Lunsford-Avery, PhD)
why: A Durham study (NCT07805382) tracking Garmin-measured sleep across menstrual cycles in adolescent girls with ADHD, alongside daily phone check-ins. Sleep timing over many nights is the core signal, and the lab is 25 minutes from us.
why_now: First posted on ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-09-04 with an estimated September 2026 start; recruiting now.
warm_path: Local Triangle network (Raleigh to Durham); Duke rows on the board are other labs, none in this group.
ask: A 20-minute chat about how they handle night-to-night sleep timing from consumer wearables, and whether early SDK docs would help future studies.
opener: Hi Matthew, I saw the new Duke study on sleep across the cycle in adolescent girls, using Garmin data.
